newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up, impact of Escondida muted.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up, impact of Escondida muted.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer in largely quiet, routine trading, the market failing to generate any strong upside momentum from a further draw in LME stocks and an anticipated walk-out at the world's biggest copper mine, Escondida in Chile.
May COMEX settled 1.25 cents firmer at 106.80 cents per pound, traded 107.50 to 106.00 cents. Spot April went out 1.05 cents higher at 107.30 cents. Volume was estimated at 7,500 lots.
LME stocks fell 7,200 tonnes this week to 152,475 tonnes, following the latest draw of 1,350 on Friday.

At 0800 local time Friday some 120 workers belonging to a small union representing less than 20 percent of the Escondida workforce went on strike. Other members of the union were expected to join their striking colleagues, labor leaders said.
Escondida management said output at the mine will not be affected, but the initial confirmation that the strike had begun prompted some shortcovering.
Brokers said the market needed to break through the key psychological $2,300 per tonne level in the LME three-months contract in order to make any decisive gains.
"How low do LME stocks have to go before we break through $2,300 per tonne," a dealer said.
Copper has been rangebound for some two weeks since a sharp selloff by funds liquidating positions. May COMEX ended just 0.35 cent firmer on the week.
The lack of volatility has also dampened arbitrage trading with LME, brokers said.
